method: Each section read in full by a machine-assisted reviewer against the packs and the ground catalogue as of this date; not a legal review.

sections.bearsOn: Defines Crown range as Crown land in a range district excluding Land Act leased land, and range development; the pack uses this to say a Land Act lease cannot carry a Range Act agreement for FPPR 44(3)(d).
Grazing and hay rights over Crown range may be granted only under this Act, FRPA or the Land Act; it fixes where a grazing right over a block can come from.
Authorizes grazing licences and permits and hay cutting licences and permits over Crown range; whether one covers the block decides the range-plan review and any FPPR 44(3)(d) argument.
A grazing licence describes its Crown range, runs 15 to 25 years and sets annual AUMs; it grants no exclusive use, which matters when FPPR 44(3)(d) is argued.
A grazing permit describes its Crown range, runs up to 10 years and sets annual AUMs.
A hay cutting licence describes its Crown range and grants the right to harvest a quantity of hay for 15 to 25 years.
A hay cutting permit grants the exclusive right to harvest a quantity of hay; exclusivity here is of hay harvest, not proof that the land is used exclusively for hay under FPPR 44(3)(d).
Minister may authorize ministry staff and agents to use Crown range to improve it; such an authorization counts for FRPA s. 51 range developments.

A range tenure does not stop the government using or granting other uses of the same Crown range, such as timber harvest, where the minister considers the use compatible with the grazing or hay rights; this is how a cutblock and a range tenure overlap.
sections.gapNote: No rule states that harvest over a range tenure rests on the minister's view that it is compatible with the grazing or hay rights, or asks whether that compatibility has been considered with the range holder.
proposedFacts: Has the district considered the proposed harvest, roads and reforestation compatible with the grazing or hay cutting rights of the range agreement over the block?

sections.bearsOn: Minister may vary a range tenure's boundary or area with the holder's consent.
Minister may delete land from a range tenure or cut AUMs for more efficient resource use, or because the range no longer supports them.
sections.gapNote: Deleting a planned block from a range tenure is a ministry decision a planner might seek; the pack does not ask whether the block has been, or should be, deleted from the tenure.
proposedFacts: Has the block area been deleted from the range agreement, or is a deletion requested, under Range Act §36 or §37?

sections.bearsOn: Minister may delete land from a range tenure where it is required for a use incompatible with grazing or hay cutting.
sections.gapNote: Where harvest and reforestation are found incompatible with grazing, deletion of the block from the range tenure is the route; no rule asks about it.
proposedFacts: Is the block land required for a use the district considers incompatible with grazing, so that it is to be deleted from the range agreement?

sections.bearsOn: A deletion or AUM reduction takes effect only after 60 days' notice, or a year's notice with an AUM cut, unless waived; this sets the lead time before a deleted block is clear of the tenure.

proposedFacts: Is a Range Act §49 directed non-use order in place, or to be requested, to keep livestock off the block while it regenerates?
